title: fix(gateway): first chats fail during cold storage startup
body:
Related: #197510

## What Problem This Solves

First chat requests can fail with storage-unavailable errors while an agent database is starting. Permissive fixture umasks also prevent Gateway tests from reaching that behavior.

## User Impact

Cold chat requests retain the existing database preparation instead of rejecting its first registration. Filesystem permission, routing, lifetime and source-identity guards remain enforced. No migration or configuration change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Wait only for an already-running first-use creator before capturing the registry witness, and classify existing-file registrations against physically qualified identities. Readiness stays in the existing fact-acquisition owner; the caller retains its lifetime and routing checks. This adds no retry or timeout increase.

Create fixture-owned `.openclaw` with mode `0700` before publishing its selectors. The native writable-ancestor guard is unchanged; no chmod, skip, quarantine or permission override is added.

## Evidence

- **Current-head integration:** PR CI [43754726962](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43754726962) and Security Review [43754726935](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/43754726935) completed successfully for `d8b5dc1572f7f53a0169de4a2d30cd9aabc9c4ef`.
- **Real first-chat flow:** [fresh isolated Gateway run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7c4c71169b62464332a11dfd9e812814) passed the additional selected case in 19.355s. A real first-use creator was paused before opening the absent target database; the same real WebSocket chat request observed a canonical startup refusal before handler work. After releasing the real creator, authorization acquired the target, `agent.wait` returned `ok`, history contained exactly one expected assistant answer, and the tracked local HTTP provider received one request. The native run ended with no suite or unhandled errors, and one-release AWS cleanup completed.

The first-chat test issues **one SDK chat intent, not one wire attempt**: the unmodified SDK made five wire attempts (four normal startup refusals, one handler start). No test retry wrapper, database prewarm or request-timeout change was added. This qualifies the current user flow with an explicit observation overlay; it is **not an original-versus-fixed Gateway RPC RED/GREEN comparison**. The owner-level causal regressions below provide that separate evidence. The provider is local and deterministic, not a live external model.

<details>
<summary>Selected first-chat native receipts and source scope</summary>

Projected from the actual selected-case and native run-end receipts; the immutable pre-release snapshot is the pause witness:

```text
published parent: d8b5dc1572f7f53a0169de4a2d30cd9aabc9c4ef
clean observation commit: 67ff49e8d5f7a748f2b180a73e0a3333e9dff550
observation tree: 319129caca8f11801330a816a249f2519f325ed9
store absent before first use: true
before release: matching target opens=1, creator paused=true
before release: canonical startup refusals=1, handler starts=0
post-release native factory increment: 1
post-release matching target increment: 3
SDK intents=1; wire attempts=5; total startup refusals=4
handler starts=1; agent.wait=ok
persisted expected answers=1; provider requests=1
selected case=passed; suite errors=0; unhandled errors=0
```

The clean native observation commit is a child of this PR head, with four explicit observation/test-path changes. The production preparer is byte-identical to the PR; the fact-reader algorithm is unchanged apart from scalar publications. It is not claimed to be the unmodified published tree. Pinned Node 24.22.1 and pinned Bun `1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1` both passed the tiny native-channel/correlation control before product work. The selected first-chat case passed; the five existing recovery cases were intentionally not selected in this additional run and are covered by the 70-case qualification below.

Only the immutable pre-release snapshot establishes the held creator. Later open counters include a normal second open; the auxiliary post-open pause flag is not a liveness observation and is excluded from qualification. Earlier probes that timed out before the required observation were rejected, not counted as causal RED.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Owner regressions, fixture isolation and scoped checks</summary>

- [Current normalized-source qualification](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_e2c94863fd1bece84bef822f7c950e59): maintained Gateway-root compiler leaf passed with all five changed files in the actual compiler program; exact five-file type-aware lint and normal `qaRuntime` build passed; all 49 owner, 16 creation/settlement and five original recovered-output cases passed (70 total, zero pending).
- [Exact first-use causal RED and original repair GREEN](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_832e9fbc61a11d78e4d264b4891c0bf5): baseline executed the first-use regression and failed with actual registry-error provenance; the initial repair passed. The normalized run requalified the later owner/readiness simplification rather than borrowing that earlier GREEN. The separate existing-store cold-registration regression also has retained original RED/fix GREEN evidence.
- [Fixture-isolation proof](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_7b92ea0a99a98574bed11207ae2637d3): permissive-umask regression failed on `0775` versus `0700`, then helper 3 + recovered-output 5 + encrypted 1 cases passed. Both fixture files remain byte-identical to that qualified source.
- Repository-configured formatting and fresh complete five-file independent review passed. All task-owned runtime leases completed one-release cleanup.

The normalized proof used failed CI merge `3449e444e4a8733541d828e894d86ce74f83705d`, with all five changed-file bytes matching this revision. Its `97dd78cc2cbd4f9dff1add734a2b316ac8d8bf31` main integration was a different whole tree; the subsequent successful current-head PR CI above, not file-byte equality, supplies integration validation.

</details>

Full-main qualification, release packaging and manual Windows/live-external-model proof are not claimed. Current-head ClawSweeper satisfaction and the native landing workflow remain required; nothing has been merged by this update.
